messages.subject: Analyzing clusters and individuals in distance for R
parts:
I have a data set of observations obtained using line transects on a driving count for mammals. Thus there is a mixture of clusters and individuals in my data. I have thus made a column named "size" and entered the size of each cluster, and in the case of individuals have put the size as 1. I am not sure however if these cluster sizes are being taken into account by the ds function (I have tested this by running a ds function with the size column and then once on the data set with the size column removed, and there was absolutely no difference between the two outcomes). Would it perhaps work better if I recorded the clusters of individuals as each being individual (so instead of having one line of distance = 10 and size = 8 I would have 8 rows of distance 10 and then no column for size)? Or am I just missing something in my data set's format? 

object Region.Label Area Sample.Label Effort distance group daytime size
1 Mahango 200 1 14 5 1    E 1
2 Mahango 200 1 14 10 1    E 12
3 Mahango 200 1 14 15 1    E 4
This is essentially how the data is set up in excel (the 1, 2, 3 should be underneath object not region.label).

Thanks.
